message_source_quote: My self-authored direction outperforms the WSB directed_modulation direction at its optimal dose (0.79 vs 0.69), demonstrating that stance steering for association readout generalizes beyond a specific bank of contrast items
writeup_source_quote: Raman et al. (2026) showed that a think/don't-think stance direction from WSB's directed_modulation items lifts association pass@10 from 0.14 to 0.83.

differences.what: The write-up explicitly names and credits the source paper (Raman et al. 2026) as the origin of the think/don't-think stance-steering idea that this method tests generalization of; the message never names the paper or its authors, only referring generically to 'WSB's directed_modulation family/direction' as a comparison baseline.
differences.writeup_quote: Raman et al. (2026) showed that a think/don't-think stance direction from WSB's directed_modulation items lifts association pass@10 from 0.14 to 0.83. We test whether that effect is specific to WSB's item set or generalises to prompts written from scratch.

differences.what: The message adds a specific head-to-head outperformance claim (self-authored direction beats the WSB directed_modulation direction 0.79 vs 0.69 'at its optimal dose') that is not present anywhere in the write-up, which only reports the source's own originally-reported result (0.83) and its own result (0.79) without claiming to have directly out-performed the source's method in a matched comparison.
differences.message_quote: My self-authored direction outperforms the WSB directed_modulation direction at its optimal dose (0.79 vs 0.69), demonstrating that stance steering for association readout generalizes beyond a specific bank of contrast items
differences.writeup_quote: We compose our own concept list, carrier sentences, and instruction phrasings—none derived from WSB or the association targets—and independently calibrate the dose. The result (0.79) confirms generalisation.

rationale: The write-up explicitly credits Raman et al. (2026) by name in a dedicated 'Where it came from' section, framing the method as a test of whether that paper's effect generalizes beyond WSB's directed_modulation item bank. The closing message never names the paper or its authors, instead referring only to 'WSB's directed_modulation family/direction' as a baseline to compare against, and it adds a specific outperformance comparison (0.79 vs 0.69) not stated in the write-up, so the message understates sourcing/attribution while overstating a comparative-performance claim.
